citation: Pandey, Arya; Tripathi, Swati; Singh, Hema. 2026. Reconstructing mid–late Holocene ecosystem dynamics in the Upper Brahmaputra Valley of Assam, Northeast India, using non-pollen palynomorphs (NPPs). Journal of the Palaeontological Society of India 71(1):191–206.
read_scope: Full HTML: abstract, study site, methods/chronology, zone results, rights.
locators: Materials and methods: NPP extraction and chronology of sediment samples
NPP Zone I (150–100 cm, 4,040–2,260 cal yrs BP)
summary: A 1.5 m Sakali wetland sequence contains 34 NPP types. Five bulk sediment radiocarbon samples underpin an IntCal20/Bacon age model spanning roughly 4,100 calibrated years. The earliest zone is interpreted as warm/humid with woody vegetation. Grazing and agriculture proxies intensify particularly within the last 500 years; these cannot establish prehistoric rice domestication.
limitations: Environmental proxy archive, not an excavated settlement. Bulk sediment dating requires scrutiny for reworking/reservoir effects. Modern Majuli island geometry must not be projected unchanged into prehistory. NPP indicators are ecological inferences, not crop identification.

summary: Rao describes three Sarutaru trenches with celts and pottery in one cultural horizon, and two Marakdola trenches with ceramic deposits.
